findings.title: Google Calendar updateEvent selectedCalendar lookup is dead code
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, the code is `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only branch that would reach the `.find()`), the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` is `cal.externalId === undefined` and will never match any element. The result is always `undefined` in that branch, so the update will run with `calendarId: undefined`, which Google will reject or default to `primary` for the wrong account. The intent (per the comment in `createEvent`) is presumably to match by `credentialId` like the new `createEvent` logic does.

findings.title: Google Calendar deleteEvent calendarId lookup is dead code
findings.body: Same defect as in `updateEvent`: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is undefined, `find` searches for `cal.externalId === undefined`, which never matches. Consequently the call falls through to `defaultCalendarId = 'primary'`, deleting the event from the organizer's primary calendar regardless of which host the reference actually belonged to. This silently destroys the wrong event on cancellation of a collective booking.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent signature change is not propagated to all implementations
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface now mandates `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`, but only `GoogleCalendarService` and `BaseCalendarService` were updated. `LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` still have the old single-argument signature, so they no longer satisfy the interface and any other third-party calendar app implementing `Calendar` will also be out of compliance. The change must either be made optional in the interface or every implementation must be updated.

findings.title: teamMember objects carry unknown firstName/lastName properties
findings.body: The new `teamMemberPromises` map returns `{ email, name, firstName: '', lastName: '', timeZone, language }`. Neither `Person` nor `TeamMember` (the element type of `CalendarEvent.team.members`) declares `firstName`/`lastName`, so these properties are excess and either cause a TypeScript error or are silently dropped. They serve no purpose in the subsequent code path (`team.members` is only iterated for `email`), and add confusion to the type. They should be removed.

findings.title: loadUsers now throws on empty dynamicUserList, breaking dynamic bookings
findings.body: The new `loadUsers` wrapper throws `HttpError(400, 'dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.')` when `!eventTypeId` and `dynamicUserList` is not an array or is empty. The previous behavior was a Prisma `findMany` that simply returned an empty array and let the caller proceed. For dynamic links/groups with no matching users (a realistic scenario, e.g. typos in slug or temporarily no active users), the booking flow now fails with a 400 instead of producing the previous, more graceful outcome. This is an unintended behavior change.

findings.title: isTeamEventType uses string literals instead of enum
findings.body: `isTeamEventType` was changed from `eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ['COLLECTIVE', 'ROUND_ROBIN'].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. Using the enum values directly (as before) is type-safe; the new string-literal array silently breaks if the enum members are ever renamed and offers no compiler protection.

findings.title: Fallback 'first connected calendar' filter never matches
findings.body: When `event.destinationCalendar` is empty, the fallback is `const [credential] = this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === 'calendar');`. Calendar credentials in this codebase have types like `google_calendar`, `office365_calendar`, etc. (all ending in `_calendar`), never a bare `'calendar'`, so the filter yields `[]`, `credential` is `undefined`, and no event is created. This is a pre-existing bug but is still present after this refactor and worth fixing while the code is being touched. A `cred.type.endsWith('_calendar')` check (matching the constructor filter) would work.

findings.title: Only the first destinationCalendar is persisted on the Booking
findings.body: The PR builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (so the loop in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` can create a Google event per host), but on persist only the first element is connected: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Prisma `Booking` model has a single `destinationCalendar` field, so subsequent code that rebuilds the array from the booking (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts` which does `[bookingToDelete?.destinationCalendar]`) will only see one calendar, even though the calendar event was actually created on multiple hosts' calendars. The PR does not include a schema change to support the array, so the asymmetry between 'events created' and 'what is stored' must be called out; downstream cancel/edit/reschedule flows will operate on the wrong subset.

findings.title: Unrelated logic change to organization create handler
findings.body: The diff inverts `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (and the same for `requestedSlug`). This is a correct fix (the old condition produced a slug only when billing was disabled), but it has nothing to do with the destinationCalendar array refactor and changes organization creation behavior. It should ideally be split into its own commit/PR so it can be reviewed and reverted independently.

findings.title: BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still expect destinationCalendar: null
findings.body: The BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was updated to `destinationCalendar: []` to match the new array contract, but the BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) tests still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The corresponding code paths in `handleNewBooking.ts` set `destinationCalendar: ... ? [...] : null` (i.e. can return either an array or `null`). A test that books a collective event type where hosts do have destination calendars configured would actually exercise the array branch and is missing from this PR; the Loom shows the new behavior but no automated test was added.
